  • Staff give no legal advice, do not decide who owns surface or mineral rights, and do not run lien searches.
  • The clerk is not required to search the records for you or vouch for their contents.

Office hours, filing cutoff and fees

Doors are open from 7:45 a.m. to 4:45 p.m. on weekdays, with no break at lunch, yet recording stops at 4 p.m. A paper that comes in after that waits for the next business day. You can pay with cash, a check or a major credit card.

Posted charges: $15 for the first page of an instrument and $4 for every page beyond it, a schedule effective January 1, 2024. E-filing into the official records goes through Simplifile, CSC or ePN. Because fees change, ask staff to verify the amount before you pay.

Work is divided among deputies. The chief deputy takes general recording, indexing and copy requests; probate, civil filings, marriage licenses and vital records each have a separate staff member and phone option. Open a call by saying you want to record a deed. Remember that clerks are not attorneys and cannot advise on what must be filed.

What Texas requires before a deed is recorded

A land conveyance can be recorded only after the owner signs it and either swears to it or acknowledges it, before two witnesses or before an officer such as a notary, county clerk, district clerk or county court judge (Property Code 12.001(b)).

The deed records hold warranty deeds of both kinds, quitclaims, trustee's, sheriff's and tax deeds, along with lien releases, affidavits and sale contracts. State law starts the fee at $5.00 for the first page and $4.00 for each additional page, then clerk charges are added, and leaving out the grantee's mailing address can cost another $25. Pay the amount Leon County posts. Before you drive to Centerville, check the online index to confirm you have the right owner name, and bring the original signed and acknowledged deed with you.

Nobody can edit an old deed to name heirs. When an owner dies, the paper depends on the situation: an executor's or administrator's deed if the estate was administered, a court order plus the will for a muniment of title, or an affidavit of heirship as the last resort.

Statewide, the valuation date is January 1, bills land in October, and the penalty-free window closes January 31. A tax lien takes hold every January 1, so a Leon County house enters any sale still owing that year's tax. Our Leon County property tax guide covers the tax office itself.

To protest a value, write to the review board by the later of May 15 or the 30th day after delivery of your notice.

Title problems in the Leon County records

The commonest one is an estate nobody opened. Where 27.9 percent of residents are 65 or older, a parent's name often remains the last owner of record, and the file then needs a legal path to the heirs.

  • A muniment of title allows a will to prove ownership when real estate liens are the only debts.
  • Heirs may file a sworn heirship statement with the Leon County Clerk, but a buyer or lender is free to ignore it.

Recording ends at 4 p.m., although the office stays open until 4:45 p.m. on weekdays. Papers that arrive later are handled the following business day.

A probate filing usually clears it. The clerk's Probate Department, at 974 East Harrison Street, 2nd Floor, Brownsville, handles probate of a will and issuance of letters testamentary, probate of a will as a muniment of title, letters of administration and determination of heirship.

What a deed needs before the clerk will record it

A deed must be an original, properly notarized or certified by the recording office of another county, state or country. It must also meet any requirements set out in Texas statute.

Under Property Code 12.001(b), a land conveyance is recordable only when signed and acknowledged, either before an authorized officer such as a notary or before two subscribing witnesses. Recordable items include warranty, special warranty, quitclaim, trustee's, sheriff's and tax deeds, plus releases, leases, contracts of sale and powers of attorney. A missing grantee mailing address can add a $25 charge.

  • Use the original signed document, not a photocopy.
  • Get the signature acknowledged by a notary or another authorized officer.
  • Include the grantee's mailing address.
  • Send the fee for the first page, added pages and any extra names.

Commissioners courts may waive land recording fees for buyers in certain grant programs, so ask the clerk whether that applies to yours.

Inheritance and probate filings

Inheritance shows up as recorded instruments that connect the owner on the old deed to the heirs. Which instrument you need depends on whether the estate went through court.

Four tools matter at the recording counter. A transfer on death deed avoids probate when it is recorded ahead of the owner's death. A muniment of title uses the court order and the will. A small estate affidavit fits estates of $75,000 or less, apart from the homestead, and needs court approval. An affidavit of heirship is a sworn statement that a title company may refuse.

  • Administered estate: an executor's or administrator's deed.
  • Will without administration: a court order and the will.
  • Transfer on death deed: record an affidavit of death with the death certificate.
  • No court action: an affidavit of heirship, which a buyer may question.

Heirs are never added to the old deed. A new instrument is recorded.

Foreclosure and tax liens

Sale notices for foreclosures go on the courthouse door and into the clerk's files at least 21 days ahead.

Sales are public auctions, held in a county-designated area between 10 a.m. and 4 p.m. on a month's first Tuesday. A borrower generally has 20 days from the default notice to reinstate. State tax liens are different. The Comptroller files notice with the county clerk, who records it in the state tax lien book, and a federal tax lien recorded with the clerk draws the $30.00 fee shown above.

Ordinary property tax liens begin each January 1 and do not show up as recorded deeds. Ask the county tax office for a tax certificate before closing; plats also need one.

Checklist before closing

Pull the deed and every recorded lien for the address, and confirm that every release has been filed. A title company will do the same, but finding a gap early saves time.

  • Search the online index for the current deed, deeds of trust, releases and affidavits.
  • Confirm that the owner on the deed matches the person selling, or record the heirship instrument first.
  • Ask the county for a tax certificate and pay delinquent taxes from proceeds if needed.
  • Look for a posted foreclosure notice if a payment has been missed.
  • Check a plat if the lot was recently divided.

Whatever is recorded against the property will surface in the buyer's title search.

Bring a government photo ID and your latest tax bill when you meet with a title company, and keep copies of every recorded document you collect along the way.

Selling an inherited or encumbered house for cash

Many Washington County sellers come to the records because something is unsettled: a parent's house with no recorded transfer, an old loan that was paid but never released, or a lien nobody remembers. A cash buyer can work with these problems, though the title company still has to clear them before it will close.

The usual order is simple. First record the instrument that puts the house in your name. Next get releases filed for any paid-off loans. Then ask the tax office for a certificate and settle any delinquent tax from your proceeds. Finally, mail or deliver the deed, with its original signature and notary acknowledgment, to the clerk in Brenham with the fee.

Because a cash sale involves no lender's underwriting, the deadline is usually set by how fast these records are cleaned up. Starting with a search of the online index, rather than a phone call to a buyer, tells you how long that will take.

Frequently asked questions

Which office takes deeds for recording in Washington County, Texas?

The Washington County Clerk, 100 East Main Street, Suite 102, Brenham, TX 77833. Mail the original signed deed with the fee, which is $25.00 for the first page.

Can I search Washington County deed records online?

Yes. Official public records are online through eDocTec, and deed records run from 1836 to the present.

What is the recording fee for a plat?

Filing a plat costs $70.00 per slide, and a copy costs $10.00. A plat needs a tax certificate showing no delinquent ad valorem taxes, among other items.

Does Washington County record transfer on death deeds?

Yes, the clerk records deeds for the county. A transfer on death deed has to be recorded before the owner dies, so file it with the clerk where the land sits.

Who do I call at the clerk's office?

Call 979-277-6216. Ask about hours, walk-in service and recording in the same call.

Deeds, liens and plats for Bell County go to the County Clerk in Belton. The Property Records/Recordings desk answers at (254) 933-5171. The clerk works from the Bell County Justice Center at 1201 Huey Road, Belton, TX 76513, weekdays from 8 in the morning to 5 in the afternoon, and takes mail at P.O. Box 480 in Belton.

Search the Official Public Records online. The clerk's main page links a SUPERSEARCH tool built on OCR and CountyFusion, along with a Property Fraud Alert sign-up. Owners of a house they seldom visit should spend the few minutes to enroll.

Before you drive to Belton, call the recording desk and confirm the document type and page count so the right fee is in hand. Staff cannot give legal advice or draft a deed, so questions about wording belong with your title company or attorney. What the clerk needs before accepting a document

The clerk takes an original notarized document or a certified copy of the original. Keep a 2 inch margin free for the stamp and instrument number.

The notary step comes from state law: real property conveyances are recordable only when signed and acknowledged, or sworn to, in front of an authorized officer. Leaving the buyer's mailing address off the deed can bring an extra $25 charge, so read that line before signing.

Send deed and address-change questions to the mapping email on its contact page. After a sale this is the step that updates the owner of record, since the district relies on the recorded deed. Protests have their own address, and the district says protests will not be accepted at any other inbox.

Each appraisal reflects who owns the property and its condition on January 1. Homestead notices go out around April 1. To protest, file by May 15 or within 30 days of the notice arriving, whichever is later. How records affect a house sale

Any claim recorded against the house appears in the title search and can hold up closing until it is paid off or released. A lien for each year's tax arises on January 1, and the person who owned the house that day remains liable for the bill after a sale.

Here is how a typical recording goes at the Belton office. The signed, notarized deed reaches the recording desk by mail, hand delivery or an approved vendor. Staff check the notary block and the margin, total the fees by page count, and stamp the instrument with its number. The district then picks up the ownership change from the recorded deed. Keep a copy of the stamped pages, because a lender or future buyer will ask for it.

Foreclosure is visible in the same records. A sale notice goes up at the courthouse, with a copy filed at the clerk's office at least 21 days beforehand. The auction itself takes place on the first Tuesday of the month between 10 a.m. and 4 p.m. The clerk's schedule lists foreclosure postings at $2.00 when the trustee does it and $12.00 when the clerk posts.

Inherited houses add another layer. Heirs often file an affidavit of heirship, a sworn statement kept by the clerk, though no buyer or lender has to rely on it. A deed that transfers property at death has to be recorded while the owner is alive, and a muniment of title order and will go to the clerk where the land lies.

Only qualified filers can. Local Government Code 195.003 limits it to groups such as attorneys, banks and title companies, working through vendors the clerk names. A homeowner mails or hand-delivers the notarized original in Belton.

Business for the day ends at 4:30 p.m., or 4:15 p.m. on a month's last business day, so deliver month-end closing documents early.

The McLennan County Clerk's office

Deed records for the county are kept by the McLennan County Clerk in Waco, on the second floor of the Records Building at 215 N 5th Street, Room 223. The counter number is 254-757-5078. It opens weekdays from 8 a.m. until 5 p.m. and closes on county holidays.

The same office also holds liens, hospital liens, cattle brands, assumed name certificates and marriage licenses, and it clerks the probate court and the commissioners' court. For a seller, one counter holds most of what a title company asks for. Staff will not interpret a document, so legal questions go to an attorney or a legal aid group.

In Texas the county clerk doubles as county recorder, and a deed is filed where the land lies. A house anywhere in McLennan County is recorded in this office, wherever its owner lives.

How far back the records go

Clerk records start in 1849 and run to the present, split between bound volumes and an electronic system. Anything recorded on or after January 1, 1996 can be searched online or on the public workstations in the clerk's office.

McLennan County Clerk record coverage
PeriodWhere the record lives

Some older deed, deed of trust and mechanic's lien volumes, from before 1996, are also reachable on office workstations. For a deed recorded before 1996, phone the clerk first and ask which format holds it.

Searching the records by name

Searches run by name. The county does not index by legal description, so you need the grantor or the grantee, meaning the seller or the buyer on the deed.

  • The Online Records Search, linked from the clerk's Official Public Records page, covers everything recorded since 1996.
  • The public workstations in the Records Building cover older volumes and anything the online tool leaves out.
  • A survey is unlikely to turn up. Surveys cannot be recorded by themselves in Texas, so the county has one only when it rode along as an exhibit to another document, which seldom happens.

Write down the volume and page, or the instrument number, of each document you locate. The title company can then order exact copies without searching again.

What the clerk requires to record a deed

The clerk posts a short list of filing standards, and a document that misses one comes back unrecorded. Only finished documents that meet them are accepted, and staff cannot advise on legal matters.

  • The land must lie in McLennan County, and any real property document needs a legal description.
  • Signatures must be originals, proved, acknowledged or sworn to as Texas law requires.
  • Only originals are accepted, apart from certified copies issued by another government agency.
  • It needs a heading naming its type, must be written in English, and must show a return address.
  • A deed also needs the grantee's address, which serves tax purposes.
  • Payment can be cash, cashier's or business checks, money orders, personal checks, or Visa, MasterCard or American Express.

Two practical points. Nobody at the counter can notarize your signature, so get the deed acknowledged beforehand. And the recorded original goes back to you by mail the next business day.

What recording costs

Leaving the grantee's mailing address off a deed can add $25. The county posts its own Recording Fee Schedule as a PDF on the Official Public Records page. Use that for the exact total, and confirm it with the clerk or title company before you write a check.

When the records show a lien, an old foreclosure or an unknown heir

The title company searches these records before closing, which is when loose ends appear. Typical finds include a mortgage paid off with no release on file, a hospital lien, a mechanic's lien, or a deed signed by a relative who has died.

  • An inherited house can be sorted out through probate, and the County Clerk keeps those case files. An affidavit of heirship can also be recorded with the clerk, but no law makes anyone accept it.

Who appraises McLennan County property, and when is a protest due?

Values for tax purposes come from the McLennan Central Appraisal District at 315 S 26th Street, Waco. A spring Notice of Appraised Value goes to owners whose market value rose by at least $1,000, and the protest deadline is May 15 or 30 days after mailing, whichever falls later.

A filed protest first gets an informal meeting with an appraiser, and an unsettled case moves to the Appraisal Review Board. Online protests for most residential property run April 10 through May 15. Homestead exemptions use Form 50-114 and are generally due by April 30.

The deed index does not show the tax bill, so a buyer should ask the McLennan County Tax Office for the account status. A tax lien attaches each January 1, and the owner that day answers for that year.

McLennan County housing at a glance

McLennan County has 272,020 people, up from 260,579 in the 2020 census, and 112,290 housing units. Owners occupy 61.8% of homes. The middle home value is $243,600, middle gross rent is $1,173 and middle household income is $66,643. Have the title company compare the recorded deed, the tax account and the seller's name early, so a mismatch surfaces well before closing. For a sale, bring a photo ID, the names of every past owner you know of, and your latest tax statement when you visit the Records Building, so staff can point you to the right index quickly.

Frequently asked questions

Can I find a McLennan County deed from a street address?

No. Records are indexed by name, not legal description, so you need the grantor or grantee. Online Records Search handles 1996 onward, and the Records Building workstations handle older volumes.

Where is the McLennan County Clerk's office?

Room 223 of the McLennan County Records Building, 215 N 5th Street, Waco, TX 76701, telephone 254-757-5078. It is open weekdays from 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. except holidays.

Can the clerk's office notarize my deed?

No. No notary works at the counter, so sign in front of a notary elsewhere and bring the original. Copies are not accepted.

Does the County Clerk run the foreclosure sale?

No, the trustee named on each notice runs it. Sales happen on the courthouse steps at 501 Washington Ave., Waco, and notices are available at the clerk's office.

How do I find out whether back taxes are owed on a McLennan County house?

Ask the McLennan County Tax Office, which treats a bill as delinquent when unpaid before February 1 of the next year. The title company's commitment will show unpaid tax as well.

Clerk's office location and hours

Photo ID to file a deed

Bring a government photo ID. Senate Bill 16, effective September 1, 2025, added Local Government Code 191.010(b). The clerk must require photo ID from whoever presents a document for the real property records, must copy it, and must reject the filing if the person refuses.

The law is a statewide deed fraud measure. It also tightens criminal penalties for real property theft and fraud, lets victims seek restitution and a no-fee judicial voiding of a fraudulent deed, and sets stronger standards for notaries. Probate and heirs

The clerk cannot recommend a route, so a Texas attorney is the person to ask which one fits the estate. Having the death certificate, the will if there is one, and a list of heirs ready speeds the first conversation.

Clay Appraisal District

The district values property and processes exemptions. It never levies, sets or collects taxes, so call the proper tax office for amounts owed. Its site, claycad.org, carries forms, an interactive map, protest hearing information and an oil and gas FAQ.

  • Over 65: the claim can be filed up to one year after the 65th birthday, with proof of age.
  • Mobile homes can be set up as improvement-only accounts if you file a request for separate taxation with the title or a verified purchase contract.

Protests are normally due May 15, or 30 days after the notice is delivered if later. A plain letter works, and no official form is required.

Clay County housing at a glance

Clay County is thinly settled: 10,764 people in the July 2025 estimate, up from 10,218 at the 2020 census, across 1,088.76 square miles. It has 5,247 housing units, and owners occupy 84.0% of 4,289 households. Owner-occupied homes have a median value of $171,500 (2020 to 2024), and gross rent has a median of $811. New construction is rare, with just 8 building permits in 2025.

With so few sales, a comparable house may be miles away. Ask a title company for recent recorded deed prices in your part of the county.

Frequently asked questions

Are Clay County property records available online?

No. Deed records are digitized back to the 1960s, but property records are not online. Call (940) 538-4631 or visit the annex in Henrietta.

What are the hours of the Clay County Clerk?

Weekdays from 7:30 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. The annex shuts for lunch from noon to 1:00 p.m., and bad weather, training or hearings can close it, so call first.

Do I need a photo ID to record a deed in Clay County?

Yes. Under Local Government Code 191.010(b), added by Senate Bill 16 effective September 1, 2025, the clerk must require photo ID from the person presenting a real property document, copy it and reject the filing if the person refuses.

How much does it cost to record a deed in Clay County?

Page one is $25 and each added page is $4. A missing grantee address, a missing heading or unreadable printed names bring extra penalties.

Who collects property tax in Clay County?

Not the appraisal district. Call the proper tax office for amounts. The appraisal district's site has a separate Pay Taxes Online link for that purpose.

Recording a deed in King County

The County Clerk in Guthrie records deeds and other land papers for King County, and the clerk's web page links to an online records search. Visit in person at 800 South Baker, or mail documents to P.O. Box 135, Guthrie, TX 79236. The phone number is 806.596.4412 and the fax is 806.596.4664.

If you mail a document, include a self-addressed envelope so the clerk can send it back. Call the office for the fee total and the hours before you put a check in the mail. Pack your envelope with these items:

  • The original deed, with ink signatures and the notary's acknowledgment
  • A mailing address for every grantee, since leaving it off can trigger an extra charge
  • An envelope addressed to yourself with postage on it
  • A check for whatever amount the clerk quotes

Which King County office does what

Three offices in Guthrie share the work on any parcel. The clerk keeps recorded documents, the chief appraiser keeps value and exemption files, and the tax assessor-collector sends statements and takes payments. Each has its own post office box.

King County offices that touch a property file

The appraisal office posts its board meeting notices on its county page, which helps if you want to know when the review board next meets.

What a deed must show before the clerk records it

A Texas clerk cannot record a land conveyance unless the signature was acknowledged or was sworn before two witnesses (Property Code 12.001(b)). The deed records take warranty deeds of both kinds, quitclaims, trustee's, sheriff's and tax deeds, lien releases, leases, powers of attorney and several kinds of affidavit.

The bill is built in layers. Page one carries $5.00 and each added page $4.00 under Local Government Code 118.012, with records management, archive and technology charges on top, within statutory caps. Every county picks its own add-ons, so the King County total will differ from the base figures. Ask the office for the whole amount.

Records follow the land. A deed for a King County house goes to Guthrie, whether the seller now lives in Lubbock, Wichita Falls or another state.

King County in brief

King County is one of the smallest counties in the nation. About 192 people live there, down from 265 in 2020 and 286 in 2010, spread over 910.87 square miles. The county has 177 housing units. Owners live in 59.5 percent of homes, and a middle-priced owned home is worth $52,100. With so few households, everything about a sale runs through Guthrie, and a call to the right office usually settles a question fast.

Record problems that come up when selling

Three snags recur: an owner who died before title was cleared, a lien nobody released, and a tax bill left unpaid. The clerk's recorded documents and the tax office files show each one, and Texas has a defined fix for each.

  • Owner died, no probate. A will may be probated within four years of death. A small estate affidavit fits only when there was no will, the assets (not counting homestead and exempt property) total $75,000 or less, and all heirs agree. A court must approve it.
  • Heirship by affidavit. A sworn heirship statement can be filed with the clerk, but no law forces a lender or title insurer to accept it.
  • Old mortgage. A paid-off lender should sign a release, and the clerk records it like any other instrument. Ask for one if the payoff happened years ago.
  • Ranch or oil acreage. When a house sits on part of a larger tract, have the title agent trace whether earlier deeds reserved minerals.

Closing agents run lien, judgment and heir searches before funds move, so these items surface early.

Property taxes and your sale

King County bills come from local taxing units, since the state levies no property tax of its own. The appraisal district prices each parcel using its January 1 status. A spring notice from the chief appraiser starts the protest clock: file by May 15, or by the 30th day after the notice reaches you if that date is later. Appeals past the review board can go to district court or binding arbitration.

Statements go out about October 1, with payment due by January 31. On February 1 an unpaid bill turns delinquent and picks up six percent in penalty plus one percent interest. The lien for each year's tax attaches on January 1, so title cannot be fully clear while a prior year remains open. The King County Tax Assessor-Collector can quote what a particular parcel owes.

Steps from records check to closing

Begin with the online search the clerk links to and look up each owner name on the deed. Note every deed of trust and whether a release follows it. Phone the tax assessor-collector for what is owed on the parcel. Then call the chief appraiser if the exemption file looks wrong. With those papers in hand, a title agent can say within a short call what stands between you and a closing.

If the problem is an estate, the title agent will usually ask for the death certificate, the will if there is one, and a list of heirs. If it is a lien, the agent asks the lender for a payoff letter and a recorded release. Most fixes are filed with the clerk in Guthrie, so a mailed packet with a return envelope often does the job without a trip.

Selling for cash when the records are messy

An as-is cash purchase can still close when the deed history needs cleanup. The title agent handles the paperwork, so you do not make repairs or host showings. Tell us what you found in the records, such as a missing heir or an old lien, and we will explain how a sale could move forward.

The closing documents are recorded with the King County Clerk afterward. The title agent confirms payoff figures on any recorded mortgage and collects taxes due at the table.

Before you call, write down the owner names on the deed, the date of any death, and the lender's name for any old loan. Those three facts shorten the first conversation with a title agent. If a will exists, mention where the original is kept.

Frequently asked questions

Who records deeds in King County, Texas?

The King County Clerk in Guthrie does. Texas makes the county clerk the county recorder, so every deed for a King County house is filed at that one office.

Can I send a deed to the King County Clerk by mail?

Yes, as long as you include a self-addressed envelope. Phone 806.596.4412 to get the fee, then mail the original signed and acknowledged deed showing a grantee mailing address.

Where do I dispute my King County appraisal?

Begin with the chief appraiser at P.O. Box 117 in Guthrie. A written protest to the appraisal review board is due May 15 or by the 30th day after the notice is delivered, whichever comes later.

What if the owner of a King County house died without probate?

Several routes exist: probating a will inside four years, a small estate affidavit for modest estates, a muniment of title, or an affidavit of heirship. The right one depends on whether a will exists and who the heirs are.

How many people live in King County, Texas?

About 192 people, down from 265 in 2020. The county has 177 housing units and a $52,100 middle value for owned homes.
